speaker_role: former admissions officer (Vassar College), now runs private admissions consulting
commercial_incentive: Yes - references private clients she coaches through the waitlist, implying a paid consulting practice
key_insights: During peak season, readers handled roughly 25-35 applications a day at about 10-12 minutes each, so first impressions and organization matter enormously
Vassar recalculated GPA on its own 12-point scale (12=A+, 11=A, etc.) rather than trusting the school-reported GPA, producing an internal 'admissions GPA'
Rigor was judged via the 'five academic food groups' (English, Math, Science, Social Science, Foreign Language); electives like art or PE generally didn't count toward the academic core unless AP
Readers cross-referenced each applicant's course choices against the high school's official school profile to see how many honors/AP/IB options were even offered, contextualizing rigor
About 60-80% of the applicant pool was judged academically qualified, meaning personal qualities (essays, recommendations, activities, community impact) were the real differentiator
In committee, admissions staff voted with colored cards (green=admit, yellow=waitlist, red=reject) and majority ruled instantly

Right before decisions were finalized, the office adjusted regional acceptance numbers to hit a target overall rate, which sometimes meant moving already-decided admits down to the waitlist without those students ever knowing
The presenter frames the process as: what is written and submitted is all that's evaluated, so the burden is on the applicant to make sure key information appears in the application
specific_numbers_or_facts: Vassar readers reviewed ~25-35 applications/day at ~10-12 minutes each (per speaker)
Vassar used a 12-point internal grading scale (12=A+, 11=A)
60-80% of the applicant pool was described as academically qualified
One year the office had to move about 30 students from admit to waitlist to correct a regional acceptance rate from 22% down to a 20% target
notable_or_distinctive: Gives a rare, specific inside account of committee mechanics (color-card voting) and the practice of quietly moving already-admitted students to the waitlist to hit yield targets.
reliability_notes: Single anecdotal account of one person's tenure at one school (Vassar) years ago; practices described (12-point recalculated GPA, card voting, last-minute regional rebalancing) may not generalize to other schools or current cycles, and cannot be independently verified from the transcript alone.
